1	# Independent Analysis of AI Models and API Providers -- Artificial Analysis, April 2026
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	- URL: https://artificialanalysis.ai/
     6	- Captured: April 10, 2026
     7	
     8	Artificial Analysis is an independent platform that benchmarks large language models across intelligence, speed, and pricing. The data below reflects the latest evaluations published in April 2026, covering both proprietary and open-weight models from major AI labs worldwide.
     9	
    10	## Intelligence Index: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Share the Lead at 57
    11	
    12	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a composite score aggregating performance across a wide range of reasoning, knowledge, and instruction-following benchmarks. Higher scores indicate stronger overall capability.
    13	
    14	As of April 2026, two models share the top position:
    15	
    16	| Rank | Model | Provider | Intelligence Index |
    17	|------|-------|----------|--------------------|
    18	| 1 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | Google | 57 |
    19	| 2 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | OpenAI | 57 |
    20	| 3 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | Anthropic | 53 |
    21	| 4 | Muse Spark | Meta | 52 |
    22	| 5 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | Anthropic | 52 |
    23	| 6 | GLM-5.1 | Z AI | 51 |
    24	| 7 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | xAI | 49 |
    25	| 8 | Gemini 3 Flash | Google | 46 |
    26	| 9 | DeepSeek V3.2 | DeepSeek | 42 |
    27	| 10 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | NVIDIA | 36 |
    28	| 11 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | OpenAI | 33 |
    29	
    30	Google and OpenAI are neck-and-neck at the frontier. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 trails by 4 points, while Meta's newly released Muse Spark enters at a strong 52. Open-weight models such as GLM-5.1 and Grok 4.20 occupy the mid-tier, demonstrating that the gap between proprietary and open-weight models continues to narrow.
    31	
    32	![Intelligence Index ranking of top AI models, April 2026](./assets/chart_intelligence_index_ranking.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Output Speed: Open-Weight Models Dominate Throughput
    35	
    36	Inference speed, measured in output tokens per second, is critical for latency-sensitive applications. The leaderboard shows a striking pattern: open-weight and smaller models generate tokens far faster than frontier proprietary models.
    37	
    38	| Rank | Model | Output Tokens/s |
    39	|------|-------|-----------------|
    40	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    41	| 2 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 188 |
    42	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 172 |
    43	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 |
    44	| 5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 118 |
    45	| 6 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 83 |
    46	| 7 | GLM-5.1 | 64 |
    47	| 8 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 63 |
    48	| 9 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 49 |
    49	| 10 | DeepSeek V3.2 | 46 |
    50	
    51	The fastest model, gpt-oss-120B (high), outputs 218 tokens per second -- more than 4x the speed of Claude Opus 4.6 and nearly 5x that of DeepSeek V3.2. This highlights the trade-off between raw intelligence and throughput: the two intelligence leaders (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4) sit in the middle of the speed table at 118 and 83 tokens/s respectively.
    52	
    53	![Output speed ranking by tokens per second](./assets/chart_output_speed_ranking.jpg)
    54	
    55	## Pricing: A 33x Gap Between Cheapest and Most Expensive
    56	
    57	API pricing per million tokens varies enormously across models, reflecting differences in compute requirements, margin strategies, and competitive positioning.
    58	
    59	| Rank | Model | USD per 1M Tokens |
    60	|------|-------|--------------------|
    61	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    62	| 2 | DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.30 |
    63	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | $0.40 |
    64	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 |
    65	| 5 | GLM-5.1 | $2.10 |
    66	| 6 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | $3.00 |
    67	| 7 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | $4.50 |
    68	| 8 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | $5.60 |
    69	| 9 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | $6.00 |
    70	| 10 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | $10.00 |
    71	
    72	The cheapest options -- gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30 per million tokens -- are over 33x less expensive than Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00. For budget-sensitive workloads, this price differential is a decisive factor. Notably, Gemini 3 Flash offers a compelling mid-range value at $1.10, pairing solid speed (153 tokens/s) with reasonable intelligence (46).
    73	
    74	![Price per million tokens comparison across models](./assets/chart_price_per_million_tokens.jpg)
    75	
    76	## The Intelligence-Throughput Frontier: Finding the "Most Attractive Quadrant"
    77	
    78	A scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus output tokens consumed during evaluation reveals which models occupy the "most attractive quadrant" -- high intelligence with efficient token usage. Models that achieve high scores while consuming fewer tokens represent better engineering and more efficient architectures.
    79	
    80	Key observations from the scatter plot:
    81	
    82	- Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and DeepSeek V3.2 cluster in the upper region, indicating strong intelligence scores.
    83	- Grok 4.20 0309 v2 and several Google models sit in the middle-right region, balancing intelligence and token efficiency.
    84	- Llama 4 Maverick occupies the low-intelligence, low-token region, suggesting it is neither efficient nor highly capable.
    85	- MiMo-V2-Pro appears in the upper-right corner, showing very high intelligence but with substantial token usage.
    86	
    87	![Scatter plot of intelligence index vs output tokens, highlighting the most attractive quadrant](./assets/chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg)
    88	
    89	## Proprietary vs. Open-Weight Models
    90	
    91	The April 2026 landscape shows proprietary models still leading on raw intelligence, but the margin is thin. GLM-5.1, an open-weight model from Z AI, scores 51 -- just 6 points behind the co-leaders. Meanwhile, open-weight models like gpt-oss-120B dominate on speed and price. The intelligence leaderboard includes models from at least 8 distinct organizations across the US, China, and Europe, reflecting a genuinely global competition.
    92	
    93	| Metric | Proprietary Leader | Score | Open-Weight Leader | Score |
    94	|--------|--------------------|-------|--------------------|-------|
    95	| Intelligence | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 57 | GLM-5.1 | 51 |
    96	| Speed (tokens/s) | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    97	| Price ($/1M tokens) | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    98	
    99	## Key Findings
   100	
   101	- **Two-way tie at the top**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (xhigh) both score 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, making them the co-leaders as of April 2026.
   102	- **Speed and intelligence are inversely correlated**: The fastest model (gpt-oss-120B at 218 tokens/s) scores only 33 on intelligence, while the smartest models operate at 49-118 tokens/s.
   103	- **Massive pricing spread**: A 33x cost gap separates the cheapest ($0.30/1M tokens for gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2) from the most expensive ($10.00/1M tokens for Claude Opus 4.6).
   104	- **Open-weight models are closing the gap**: GLM-5.1 at 51 intelligence is within 10% of the proprietary leaders, while also being significantly cheaper at $2.10/1M tokens.
   105	- **No single model wins on all three axes**: Choosing a model requires explicit trade-offs among intelligence, speed, and cost depending on the use case.

    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```
   255	
   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```

   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE

# Create presentation with 16:9 aspect ratio
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette - professional, data-forward
DARK_BLUE = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x23, 0x7E)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
LIGHT_BLUE = RGBColor(0xE6, 0xF0, 0xFA)
DARK_GRAY = RGBColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
ORANGE = RGBColor(0xE6, 0x5C, 0x00)
GREEN = RGBColor(0x28, 0x7A, 0x3E)

def add_title_slide(prs, title, subtitle):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    
    # Background shape
    bg = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height)
    bg.fill.solid()
    bg.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
    bg.line.fill.background()
    
    # Title
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.75), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.8), Inches(2))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(40)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    
    # Subtitle
    sub_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.75), Inches(4.4), Inches(11.8), Inches(1))
    tf = sub_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = subtitle
    p.font.size = Pt(20)
    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xAA, 0xCC, 0xFF)
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    
    # Source line
    src_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.75), Inches(6.5), Inches(11.8), Inches(0.5))
    tf = src_box.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Source: Artificial Analysis  |  April 2026"
    p.font.size = Pt(12)
    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0xBB)
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    
    return slide

def add_content_slide(prs, title, content_elements):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    
    # Top accent bar
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, Inches(0.15))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_BLUE
    bar.line.fill.background()
    
    # Title
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(28)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
    
    y_pos = Inches(1.3)
    for elem in content_elements:
        elem_type = elem.get('type')
        if elem_type == 'text':
            box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), y_pos, Inches(12), elem.get('height', Inches(0.5)))
            tf = box.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = elem['text']
            p.font.size = Pt(elem.get('size', 14))
            p.font.color.rgb = elem.get('color', DARK_GRAY)
            p.alignment = elem.get('align', PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
            if elem.get('bold', False):
                p.font.bold = True
            y_pos += elem.get('height', Inches(0.5)) + Inches(0.1)
        elif elem_type == 'table':
            rows = elem['rows']
            cols = elem['cols']
            data = elem['data']
            col_widths = elem.get('col_widths', None)
            
            table_width = Inches(12)
            table_height = Inches(len(rows) * 0.38 + 0.3)
            table = slide.shapes.add_table(len(rows), len(cols), Inches(0.6), y_pos, table_width, table_height).table
            
            if col_widths:
                for i, w in enumerate(col_widths):
                    table.columns[i].width = Inches(w)
            
            for r_idx, row in enumerate(rows):
                for c_idx in range(len(cols)):
                    cell = table.cell(r_idx, c_idx)
                    cell.text = str(data[r_idx][c_idx])
                    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
                    p.font.size = Pt(11)
                    p.font.color.rgb = DARK_GRAY
                    if r_idx == 0 or elem.get('bold_first_col', False) and c_idx == 0:
                        p.font.bold = True
                    if r_idx == 0:
                        p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
                        cell.fill.solid()
                        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
                    else:
                        if r_idx % 2 == 0:
                            cell.fill.solid()
                            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = LIGHT_BLUE
                        else:
                            cell.fill.solid()
                            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = WHITE
            y_pos += table_height + Inches(0.2)
        elif elem_type == 'chart':
            chart_data = CategoryChartData()
            chart_data.categories = elem['categories']
            chart_data.add_series(elem['series_name'], elem['values'])
            
            chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
                elem['chart_type'],
                Inches(0.6), y_pos,
                Inches(12), Inches(4.2),
                chart_data
            ).chart
            
            chart.has_legend = True
            chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
            if elem.get('chart_title'):
                chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = elem['chart_title']
            y_pos += Inches(4.5)
        elif elem_type == 'image':
            slide.shapes.add_picture(
                elem['path'],
                Inches(0.6), y_pos,
                width=Inches(elem.get('width', 12))
            )
            y_pos += Inches(elem.get('height', 4)) + Inches(0.2)
        elif elem_type == 'bullets':
            box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), y_pos, Inches(12), elem.get('height', Inches(2)))
            tf = box.text_frame
            tf.word_wrap = True
            for i, bullet in enumerate(elem['items']):
                if i == 0:
                    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
                else:
                    p = tf.add_paragraph()
                p.text = bullet
                p.font.size = Pt(elem.get('size', 14))
                p.font.color.rgb = DARK_GRAY
                p.level = 0
                p.space_after = Pt(8)
            y_pos += elem.get('height', Inches(2)) + Inches(0.1)
    
    return slide

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 1: Title
# ============================================================
add_title_slide(prs,
    "AI Model Landscape April 2026: Benchmarking Intelligence, Speed, and Cost Across 11 Frontier Models",
    "Independent analysis from Artificial Analysis  |  April 2026")

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 2: Intelligence
# ============================================================
intelligence_data = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "Provider", "Intelligence Index"],
    [1, "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "Google", 57],
    [2, "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "OpenAI", 57],
    [3, "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "Anthropic", 53],
    [4, "Muse Spark", "Meta", 52],
    [5, "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "Anthropic", 52],
    [6, "GLM-5.1", "Z AI", 51],
    [7, "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "xAI", 49],
    [8, "Gemini 3 Flash", "Google", 46],
    [9, "DeepSeek V3.2", "DeepSeek", 42],
    [10, "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "NVIDIA", 36],
    [11, "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "OpenAI", 33],
]

intelligence_rows = [intelligence_data[0]] + intelligence_data[1:]
intelligence_elements = [
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Google and OpenAI are neck-and-neck at the frontier. Anthropic\'s Claude Opus 4.6 trails by 4 points, while Meta\'s newly released Muse Spark enters at a strong 52. Open-weight models such as GLM-5.1 and Grok 4.20 occupy the mid-tier, demonstrating that the gap between proprietary and open-weight models continues to narrow.', 'size': 14, 'height': Inches(0.7)},
    {'type': 'table', 'rows': intelligence_rows, 'cols': ['Rank', 'Model', 'Provider', 'Score'], 'data': intelligence_rows, 'col_widths': [1.0, 4.2, 2.8, 2.2]},
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Spread: 57 (co-leaders) to 33 (gpt-oss-120B)  |  8 organizations across US, China, and Europe', 'size': 12, 'color': MEDIUM_GRAY, 'height': Inches(0.3)},
]
add_content_slide(prs, "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Co-Lead the Intelligence Index at 57", intelligence_elements)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 3: Speed
# ============================================================
speed_data = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "Output Tokens/s"],
    [1, "gpt-oss-120B (high)", 218],
    [2, "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", 188],
    [3, "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", 172],
    [4, "Gemini 3 Flash", 153],
    [5, "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", 118],
    [6, "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", 83],
    [7, "GLM-5.1", 64],
    [8, "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", 63],
    [9, "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", 49],
    [10, "DeepSeek V3.2", 46],
]

speed_rows = [speed_data[0]] + speed_data[1:]
speed_elements = [
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'The fastest model, gpt-oss-120B (high), outputs 218 tokens per second -- more than 4x the speed of Claude Opus 4.6 and nearly 5x that of DeepSeek V3.2. This highlights the trade-off between raw intelligence and throughput: the two intelligence leaders (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4) sit in the middle of the speed table at 118 and 83 tokens/s respectively.', 'size': 14, 'height': Inches(0.7)},
    {'type': 'table', 'rows': speed_rows, 'cols': ['Rank', 'Model', 'Tokens/s'], 'data': speed_rows, 'col_widths': [1.2, 5.5, 2.0]},
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Note: Muse Spark has no published speed data in this benchmark.', 'size': 12, 'color': MEDIUM_GRAY, 'height': Inches(0.3)},
]
add_content_slide(prs, "gpt-oss-120B Tops Output Speed at 218 Tokens/s -- More Than 4x Faster Than Claude Opus 4.6", speed_elements)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 4: Pricing
# ============================================================
pricing_data = [
    ["Rank", "Model", "USD per 1M Tokens"],
    [1, "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "$0.30"],
    [2, "DeepSeek V3.2", "$0.30"],
    [3, "NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super", "$0.40"],
    [4, "Gemini 3 Flash", "$1.10"],
    [5, "GLM-5.1", "$2.10"],
    [6, "Grok 4.20 0309 v2", "$3.00"],
    [7, "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "$4.50"],
    [8, "GPT-5.4 (xhigh)", "$5.60"],
    [9, "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max)", "$6.00"],
    [10, "Claude Opus 4.6 (max)", "$10.00"],
]

pricing_rows = [pricing_data[0]] + pricing_data[1:]
pricing_elements = [
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'The cheapest options -- gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30 per million tokens -- are over 33x less expensive than Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00. For budget-sensitive workloads, this price differential is a decisive factor. Notably, Gemini 3 Flash offers a compelling mid-range value at $1.10, pairing solid speed (153 tokens/s) with reasonable intelligence (46).', 'size': 14, 'height': Inches(0.7)},
    {'type': 'table', 'rows': pricing_rows, 'cols': ['Rank', 'Model', 'Price/1M'], 'data': pricing_rows, 'col_widths': [1.2, 5.5, 2.0]},
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Note: Muse Spark has no published pricing data in this benchmark.', 'size': 12, 'color': MEDIUM_GRAY, 'height': Inches(0.3)},
]
add_content_slide(prs, "From $0.30 to $10 per Million Tokens: A 33x Pricing Gap Across Models", pricing_elements)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 5: Trade-offs
# ============================================================
tradeoff_elements = [
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'A scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus output tokens consumed during evaluation reveals which models occupy the "most attractive quadrant" -- high intelligence with efficient token usage.', 'size': 14, 'height': Inches(0.5)},
    {'type': 'image', 'path': '/app/benchmark/assets/chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg', 'width': 7.5, 'height': 4.5},
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Key insight: No single model dominates all three axes. Choosing a model requires explicit trade-offs among intelligence, speed, and cost.', 'size': 13, 'bold': True, 'color': DARK_BLUE, 'height': Inches(0.4)},
    {'type': 'table', 'rows': [
        ["Metric", "Proprietary Leader", "Score", "Open-Weight Leader", "Score"],
        ["Intelligence", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "57", "GLM-5.1", "51"],
        ["Speed (tokens/s)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "153", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "218"],
        ["Price ($/1M tokens)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "$1.10", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "$0.30"],
    ], 'cols': ['Metric', 'Proprietary', 'Score', 'Open-Weight', 'Score'], 'data': [
        ["Metric", "Proprietary Leader", "Score", "Open-Weight Leader", "Score"],
        ["Intelligence", "Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview", "57", "GLM-5.1", "51"],
        ["Speed (tokens/s)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "153", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "218"],
        ["Price ($/1M tokens)", "Gemini 3 Flash", "$1.10", "gpt-oss-120B (high)", "$0.30"],
    ], 'col_widths': [2.5, 3.0, 1.5, 3.0, 1.5], 'bold_first_col': True},
]
add_content_slide(prs, "No Model Wins on All Three Axes: Navigating the Intelligence-Efficiency-Cost Frontier", tradeoff_elements)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 6: Takeaways
# ============================================================
takeaway_elements = [
    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Key findings and recommendations for AI engineering leads and product managers:', 'size': 14, 'height': Inches(0.4)},
    {'type': 'bullets', 'items': [

    {'type': 'text', 'text': 'Recommendation: Prioritize intelligence for research and complex reasoning tasks; prioritize speed for real-time applications; prioritize cost for high-volume, budget-sensitive deployments.
